This file exists so that any AI agent with shell access to this folder can
work with it correctly on the first try, without asking a human to explain
the conventions first. It describes **this vault specifically** — the facts
below come from this vault's own `vault.yaml` and file tree, not from Kagaz
in general. For how Kagaz's conventions and tooling work in the abstract,
see [the project docs](https://getkagaz.github.io/kagaz/), in particular
[docs/agents.md](https://getkagaz.github.io/kagaz/agents.html) and
[docs/conventions-guide.md](https://getkagaz.github.io/kagaz/conventions-guide.html).

## The two ways to interact with this vault

1. **`kagaz --json` from a shell.** Every command supports `--json` with a
   stable, documented shape. This is the primary interface for an agent —
   nothing is held back from a shell-only caller.
2. **The `kagaz mcp` server**, if the environment you're running in speaks
   MCP: `find`, `ingest_propose`, `tag`, `resolve_for_send`, returning the
   same JSON shapes as the CLI.

**Read this file before acting on this vault, but call `kagaz --json`
(`find`, `lint`, `doctor`) for anything current** — this file is
regenerated on demand, not live; a `kagaz find --json` result is always
more current than a stale fact repeated here.

## Filename grammar

Every conventionally named document in this vault follows:

```
{DocType}_{Names}_{Identifier}[_{Year}][_{Modifier}]
```

Fields are joined with `_`; words *within* a field
(an owner's name, an identifier) are joined with `-`.
A name outside this grammar is a `kagaz lint` finding, not necessarily a
bad file — real vaults accumulate files Kagaz did not create.

## Folder layout

| Category | Folder | Layout | Documents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `financial` | `Financial/` | `{Owner}/{FY}` | 3 |
| `identity` | `Identity/` | `{Owner}` | 1 |
| `travel` | `Travel/` | `{Owner}` | 1 |

A category's `layout` may include an `{Owner}` segment (the owner's display
name run through the same word-separator normalization as inside a
filename — spaces become `-`, so a person is a
literal folder component, never containing a raw space) and/or an `{FY}`
segment (the fiscal-year label, **not** normalized — its own spaces are
kept as written). The fiscal year is the calendar year (it starts in January) and is labelled `FY 2026`, which is also the `{FY}` folder name and the `fy2026` tag.

## Retrieval patterns

Prefer `kagaz find --json` over walking the tree yourself — it already
knows this vault's filters, applies the mdfind accelerator when available,
and returns parsed facts (owner, doctype, year, tags) alongside each path:

```
kagaz find --doctype invoice --person "<name>" --period FY2026 --json
kagaz find --tag confidential --json
kagaz find "acme" --json
```

If you need to query outside Kagaz entirely (Spotlight directly, or another
tool that shells out to `mdfind`), these smart-folder queries match this
vault's own tag vocabulary:

```
# every document carrying a lifecycle tag
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "active"c'
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "confidential"c'
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "dont-touch"c'
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "encrypted"c'
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "superseded"c'
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "to-action"c'

# by area
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "tax"c'

# by person, company or fiscal year: substitute a tag from the vocabulary above
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "<tag>"c'

# two tags at once (this vault's tags are ANDed, like kagaz find --tag a --tag b)
mdfind -onlyin . 'kMDItemUserTags == "<tag>"c && kMDItemUserTags == "<other-tag>"c'

# free text in a document's indexed contents or its name
mdfind -onlyin . '(kMDItemTextContent == "*<text>*"cd || kMDItemDisplayName == "*<text>*"cd)'
```

## Invariants that hold no matter how you connect

- **Nothing you do here reaches the network.** Classification and OCR run
  on-device; the only network call anywhere in Kagaz is an explicit, human-
  run `kagaz model pull`.
- **Every mutation previews before it commits** and needs explicit approval
  (`--yes`/`--accept-proposal` on the CLI, or the equivalent MCP argument).
  `--propose-only` always exits without mutating.
- **A document tagged `confidential` cannot be resolved for external send
  without explicit confirmation**, and an audit line is written either way
  — there is no flag or JSON mode that skips either. See
  [docs/commands.md#resolve---for-send](https://getkagaz.github.io/kagaz/commands.html#resolve---for-send).
- **No MCP tool executes a mutation on its own.** `ingest_propose` returns a
  proposal; a human (or the CLI, driven by a human's explicit approval)
  executes it. This friction is deliberate, not a missing feature.
- **A vault document is never deleted.** A "move" relocates the file into
  its conventional place and retires the source into a staging folder only
  the vault's owner empties.
- **Every mutation is reversible** via `kagaz rollback <manifest>`.
